findings.description: bunker_mode_active is listed as an input but has no companion freshness timestamp field (e.g. bunker_mode_last_update_ts_ms) in the inputs section and no bunker_mode_max_age_ms in the §2.2.1.2 freshness-defaults table. Line 485 says MarketIntegrityAxis is STRESSED when bunker_mode_active 'exceeds its staleness threshold per §2.2.1.2', but §2.2.1.2 only defines mm_util_max_age_ms and disk_used_max_age_ms. There is no threshold to exceed — the staleness check is unimplementable as written.

evidence.quote: - `STRESSED` if `bunker_mode_active` is missing, unparseable, or exceeds its staleness threshold per §2.2.1.2 (fail-closed).
evidence.context: Input list at line 19 defines `bunker_mode_active (bool)` with no _ts_ms pair. Freshness defaults at lines 198-199 list only mm_util_max_age_ms and disk_used_max_age_ms.

findings.proposed_fix: Add `bunker_mode_last_update_ts_ms` to the inputs section and add `bunker_mode_max_age_ms` to the §2.2.1.2 freshness defaults table (with a default value, e.g. 10_000 ms). AT-1249 already tests the stale case but the implementation cannot pass without the field and threshold defined.

findings.description: The field rename transition rule (lines 37-42) mandates MUST-level behavior: implementations MUST accept both `rate_limit_session_kill_active` and `session_termination_active` while running contract version 5.2, and MUST remove the old name in the next version. No acceptance test exists to verify dual-name acceptance or that the old name is correctly ignored after transition.

evidence.quote: - Implementations MUST accept both field names while running contract version `5.2`.
evidence.context: Lines 37-42 define a complete normative transition protocol. No AT-### entry covers this. AT-1068/AT-348 test session_termination_active signal behavior but not the aliasing.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an AT: Given contract_version=5.2, when a payload uses the old field name `rate_limit_session_kill_active=true`, PolicyGuard MUST treat it as `session_termination_active=true` and compute Kill. Pass: Kill computed. Fail: field ignored, Active returned.

findings.description: Two safety-critical resolution rules use SHALL instead of MUST. Line 412: 'PolicyGuard SHALL compute TradingMode from three independent health axes' and line 513: 'TradingMode...SHALL be computed from axes by the following rules (no other rules are permitted).' The parenthetical '(no other rules are permitted)' signals non-negotiable intent, but SHALL is weaker than MUST under RFC 2119 and is inconsistent with the contract's normative language elsewhere.

evidence.quote: TradingMode ∈ { `Active`, `ReduceOnly`, `Kill` } SHALL be computed from axes by the following rules (no other rules are permitted):
evidence.context: All other safety-critical rules in this section use MUST. SHALL at a computation rule that admits no exceptions is an inconsistency that could be cited to justify deviation.

findings.proposed_fix: Replace 'SHALL' with 'MUST' at lines 412 and 513. The parenthetical at line 513 already expresses non-negotiable intent; align the modal verb.

findings.description: AT-931 (line 747) requires 'dispatch count remains 0 and reject reason indicates TradingMode gate' as its pass criterion, implying a RejectReasonCode for TradingMode-blocked OPEN. No such code exists in the §2.2.6 registry (lines 1082-1111). AT-1101 mandates 1:1 correspondence between contract rejection tokens and code enum variants, so AT-931's requirement creates an untestable state: passing AT-931 requires a code that violates the registry's completeness.

evidence.quote: - Pass criteria: dispatch count remains 0 and reject reason indicates TradingMode gate.
evidence.context: Registry at lines 1082-1111 has no TradingModeBlockedOpen or equivalent entry. The closest entry is RiskIncreasingCancelReplaceForbidden which is a different rejection category.

findings.proposed_fix: Add `TradingModeBlockedOpen` (or equivalent) to the §2.2.6 RejectReasonCode registry and update AT-931 pass criteria to reference the exact token. Alternatively, clarify that TradingMode blockage is not emitted as a RejectReasonCode and remove that claim from AT-931's pass criteria.

findings.section: 2.2.4 Open Permission Latch — AT-1243 duplicate ID
findings.description: AT-1243 is used for two distinct tests: line 954 (reconciliation stall observability test) and line 1037 (runtime-binding cert concurrent with reconcile-class reason code test). Duplicate AT IDs break traceability, make automated AT-lookup tools return wrong tests, and prevent unambiguous reference from PRD items or code.

evidence.context: AT-1243 first appears at line 954 as the reconcile-stall observability AT. It reappears at line 1037 for a different scenario (concurrent cert failure + reconcile-class codes). Both are distinct tests that need distinct IDs.

findings.proposed_fix: Renumber the AT at line 1037 to a unique ID (e.g. AT-1251). Update any PRD or TRACE.yaml references to the old ID.

findings.description: The SystemIntegrityAxis DEGRADED predicate includes `fee_model_cache_age_s > fee_model_hard_stale_s` (line 502), producing REDUCEONLY_FEE_MODEL_HARD_STALE. No acceptance test in this section validates this specific predicate. The only fee-related entry is `FeeCacheStale` in the RejectReasonCode registry and a reason-code registry entry at line 631, but there is no AT proving that exceeding fee_model_hard_stale_s actually forces ReduceOnly with that reason code.

evidence.context: REDUCEONLY_FEE_MODEL_HARD_STALE appears in the reason-code registry at line 631. No Given/When/Then test block covers this predicate in §2.2 or §2.2.3.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an AT: Given `fee_model_cache_age_s > fee_model_hard_stale_s` and all other gates pass, When TradingMode is computed, Then TradingMode==ReduceOnly and mode_reasons includes REDUCEONLY_FEE_MODEL_HARD_STALE. Pass: OPEN blocked. Fail: Active returned or reason missing.

findings.description: `cortex_override` is a capital-critical Kill input (CapitalRiskAxis CRITICAL when ForceKill) and a ReduceOnly input (ForceReduceOnly). The §2.2.1.2 critical inputs list (lines 192-195) does not include `cortex_override`, and no rule specifies what PolicyGuard MUST do when `cortex_override` is missing or unparseable. If it defaults to None/absent, a corrupted ForceKill signal could be silently dropped — a fail-open risk.

evidence.quote: **Critical inputs (definition):** any PolicyGuard input referenced by §2.2.3 axis predicates that is required under the current `enforced_profile`.
evidence.context: cortex_override drives CapitalRiskAxis CRITICAL (line 477) and SystemIntegrityAxis DEGRADED (line 501), yet it has no companion _ts_ms field, no max-age, and no explicit missing/unparseable handling rule. AT-413 covers 'each critical input... one at a time' but cortex_override is not listed as a critical input.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit rule: if `cortex_override` is missing or unparseable, PolicyGuard MUST treat it as `ForceReduceOnly` (fail-closed) and include REDUCEONLY_INPUT_MISSING_OR_STALE. Add a corresponding AT covering the missing/unparseable case.

findings.section: 2.2.4 Open Permission Latch — reconciliation REST failure
findings.description: Line 944 requires that if the REST `/get_user_trades` query fails (network error, timeout, HTTP error, or unparseable response), reconciliation MUST fail closed and the latch MUST remain set. AT-1100 covers the case where the REST query returns trades missing from the local ledger, but no AT covers the case where the REST query itself fails (transport/HTTP error). This is a separate fail-closed path with no AT coverage.

evidence.quote: If the REST query fails (network error, timeout, HTTP error, or unparseable response), reconciliation MUST fail closed — the latch MUST remain set and OPEN intents MUST remain blocked.
evidence.context: AT-1100 (line 962) covers missing-trades, not REST failure. The fail-closed on REST failure is a MUST-level requirement with no dedicated AT.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an AT: Given open_permission_blocked_latch==true and the REST /get_user_trades call returns a network error/timeout/HTTP error/unparseable response, When reconciliation success criteria are evaluated, Then reconciliation MUST fail and latch MUST remain true. Pass: latch stays set. Fail: reconciliation succeeds or latch clears.

findings.description: The Recovery Rule (lines 565-570) states 'Axis recovery MUST be slower than axis degradation' and lists four specific hysteresis/cooldown mechanisms. This is a MUST-level normative rule but has no dedicated acceptance test. AT-1053 tests monotonicity (worse axes → not less restrictive) but does not test the recovery direction: that a recovering axis does not produce a less-restrictive mode faster than the hysteresis windows allow.

evidence.quote: - Axis recovery MUST be slower than axis degradation. Recovery MUST respect the hysteresis/cooldown rules of each producer:
evidence.context: The four listed recovery mechanisms (EvidenceGuard §2.2.2, Bunker Mode §2.3.2, Emergency ReduceOnly, Open Permission Latch §2.2.4) each have their own cooldown ATs but no AT proves the cross-cutting 'recovery is slower than degradation' invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an AT: Given a ReduceOnly trigger activates and then immediately clears (sub-cooldown), When TradingMode is computed on the next tick, Then TradingMode MUST NOT return to Active until the applicable hysteresis window has elapsed. Pass: ReduceOnly held during hysteresis. Fail: Active returned before hysteresis expires.

findings.description: Line 30 states `emergency_reduceonly_active` 'automatically clears to false after cooldown duration expires AND reconciliation confirms exposure is safe (if reconciliation is required by trigger source).' The qualifier 'if reconciliation is required by trigger source' is not defined anywhere in §2.2 — no enumeration of which trigger sources require reconciliation and which do not. An implementer could choose to never require reconciliation, allowing the flag to clear on cooldown alone in all cases.

evidence.quote: automatically clears to false after cooldown duration expires AND reconciliation confirms exposure is safe (if reconciliation is required by trigger source).
evidence.context: No table or list in §2.2 or elsewhere in this fixture enumerates which emergency-reduceonly trigger sources require reconciliation before clearing. AT-132 (line 775) repeats '(if required)' without disambiguating.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a normative table enumerating emergency-reduceonly trigger sources and whether each requires reconciliation before clearing (e.g. POST /api/v1/emergency/reduce_only → reconciliation required; or specify that all sources require reconciliation, making the qualifier unconditional). This removes the ambiguity without changing the existing behavior.
